newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY CA TO MERGE MATURING FUND WITH NEWER FUND.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY CA TO MERGE MATURING FUND WITH NEWER FUND.

text.p: Hungary's Creditanstalt Securities Investment Fund Management Ltd said it was merging its maturing closed-end fund with one of its open-ended funds to avoid losses stemming from the liquidation of the fund.
The five-year CA Securities Hungarian Government Debt Fund (CALAP) -- Hungary's first ever investment fund -- was scheduled to terminate on April 9, 1997.

"We decided not to let the fund (CALAP) mature but to merge it into the CA Fixed Income Fund (CAKAL) which was launched in January," Csaba Lantos, director for fund management at Creditanstalt Securities, told a news conference on Thursday.

According to Hungarian law, the portfolio of a terminated fund must be put on a non-interest bearing deposit account and held there until all the assets are liquidated and the Hungarian Banking and Capital Market Supervision authorises the distribution of the proceeds.
CA said in a statement this process could take months.
The exchange rate between the two funds is based on the April 4, 1997, net asset values of the respective funds, the statement said.
As a result of the merger the owners of the terminated fund will be entitled to the applicable amount of investment units of the new fund.
Lantos said the maturing fund saw above-inflation yields in every year except 1993.
"This proved to be an investment which surpassed inflation by an annual average of five percent," he added.
